`transition: all` animates every animatable property (including layout-affecting ones and inherited/injected values). The loader module is both statically imported here and registered via `register()` below. The static import is documented as an intentional traceable dependency edge for the Fallow audit, but it also *evaluates* the loader module in the main thread (constructing `vitePreprocess()` at line 12 of the loader) purely as a side effect. Consider replacing the side-effecting static import with a `// fallow` pragma or a re-export that Fallow can trace without executing the module, to avoid duplicated loader work and confusion about double registration.

Spec imports run at top level with no error handling; if a spec throws during import (e.g. a syntax/Svelte compile error), the process aborts with an unhandled rejection stack trace and `mocha.run` never executes, so there is no aggregated failure report and the exit code comes from Node's default rather than the harness. Wrapping the loader registration and spec imports in try/catch (printing a clear error and `process.exit(1)`) would give a reliable failure signal.

`mocha.run`'s callback only distinguishes failures > 0. Failures emitted via the `'end'`/uncaught-exception path, or a run that never reaches the callback, are not handled here, and the `'error'` behavior of Mocha (abrupt exit) is left to defaults. Consider also handling the run's error/abort cases explicitly so non-test runtime errors surface with a non-zero exit code rather than silently succeeding.

`probeExtensions` catches every error from `nextResolve` and treats it as "try the next extension". Because a real resolution failure (e.g. a permission error, a malformed package export map, or a genuine module-not-found inside a resolvable candidate) is indistinguishable from a simple mismatch, the caller silently falls through and Node later reports "module not found" for the *original* specifier with no hint that a candidate was found but failed. Consider only swallowing `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` and re-throwing anything else so real failures surface with their original context.

`needsExtensionProbe` whitelists only `.ts`, `.js`, `.json`, so a specifier that already ends in `.svelte`, `.mjs` or `.cjs` still triggers a probe. In the resolve flow `.svelte` specifiers short-circuit earlier, but `.mjs`/`.cjs` siblings (which this loader can never resolve since the candidate extensions are `.ts`/`.js`/`.svelte`) still incur up to three failing `nextResolve` round-trips each time. Add the actually-resolvable extensions to the check to avoid the wasted probing.

The `browser` condition is appended to the resolution conditions for every specifier that falls through (not just `svelte`/`esm-env`), despite the comment scoping the intent to the client runtime. This globally shifts Node resolution for unrelated packages, which can silently load browser-only builds (or fail on packages without a browser condition) and diverge from the plain-Node runtime the tests are meant to exercise. Consider restricting the injected condition to the packages that need it, or documenting why global injection is required.

`resolvePath(parentDirOf(context), specifier)` and `pathToFileURL(base + ext)` concatenate the raw specifier with the parent dir without validating traversal or scheme. A relative specifier such as `../../foo` escapes the parent directory and is silently accepted. For a test-only loader this is low risk, but a short guard (reject specifiers containing `..` segments or non-relative schemes) would keep resolution scoped and make the intent explicit.

`load` performs `readFileSync`, `preprocess` and `compile`/`compileModule` without any error handling. Keeping the strict type for consumers is fine, but the `typeConfig`/`data-type` fallbacks are currently the only runtime guard.

`item.text` is only surfaced via the `title` attribute, and `.activity-pill` truncates with `text-overflow: ellipsis` / `max-width: 280px`. Because the pill is a plain `<span>`, `title` is the only carrier of the full text — it is not reliably announced by all screen readers and is unreachable by keyboard (the pill is not focusable), so a truncated status is effectively inaccessible. Provide the full text in the DOM (visible or `visually-hidden`/`aria-label`) rather than relying solely on `title`.

The `extension` type is labeled `"pkg"`. For an activity bar whose types are `extension` / `tool` / `system`, a `pkg` label is inconsistent and misleading to users (a package is not the same thing as an extension). Consider `"ext"` (or the full `"extension"`) so the label matches the type it represents.

comments.content: `selectedProvider` is not reset when the selected provider disappears from `providerNames` (e.g., after `onRefresh` removes/unconfigures a provider, or when the previously chosen provider's models are removed). In that case `selectedProvider` holds a stale value that is no longer rendered as a chip, `filteredModels` stays permanently empty, and the empty list offers no obvious recovery cue. Reset/clamp the selection whenever providerNames changes.

The `if (!configuredModels) return [];` guard is dead code: `configuredModels` is a `$derived` value that is always an array (result of `models.filter(...)`), so it can never be nullish. It adds a misleading impression that `configuredModels` may be undefined. Also note that the `models` prop itself is not guarded, so if a caller passes `undefined` for `models` the earlier `$derived` at `configuredModels` would already throw. Consider guarding the props instead.

Chips do not expose selection state to assistive technology. The visual `.chip.active` class conveys the active provider, but there is no `aria-pressed` (or radiogroup/role) so screen-reader users cannot tell which filter is active. Add `aria-pressed={selectedProvider === provider}` for consistency with the model items.

              class:active={selectedProvider === provider}

comments.content: The favorite button inside the clickable `role="button"` item has no accessible name: it relies solely on `title`, which is not reliably announced by screen readers, and the SVG has no `aria-hidden`. Provide an `aria-label` (and mark the decorative SVG as `aria-hidden="true"`). Also note the keyboard path (Enter/Space on the outer item) calls `selectModel`, while the fav button has no keyboard-specific defect but the title-only labeling reduces accessibility.

`searchQuery` is lowercased before comparison but the searchable fields are compared case-insensitively only on the substring; that part is fine. However, the input is not trimmed for the provider filter, and more importantly `selectedProvider` filter is applied before search, which is acceptable. The real concern: search matches `m.name` and `m.provider` but not `m.id`, while `onSelect`/favorites operate on `m.id`; this is a minor mismatch but could confuse users searching by id. Confirm whether id search is expected.

Performance: `favoriteModels.includes(model.id)` is evaluated multiple times per item (in `class:active`, `title`, and `fill`), giving O(n*m) behavior across the list. Convert `favoriteModels` to a derived `Set` once and reuse it for O(1) lookups, especially as the model list and favorites grow.

The deferred `setTimeout(() => onClose(), 2000)` is never cleared on unmount. If the user closes the dialog (Escape / outside-click / Cancel) before the 2s elapses, the timer still fires and calls `onClose()` against an already-destroyed component, which can throw or double-fire the parent's close handler. Store the timer id and clear it in the `$effect` cleanup, matching the existing pattern used in `Toast.svelte`/`PiPackagesPanel.svelte`.

There is no timeout or reset path for the `exporting` state, and the `try/catch` around `sendMessage` is misleading: `postToHost` is synchronous and silently no-ops when `window.vscode.postMessage` is unavailable, so it never throws synchronously and the real failure surfaces asynchronously via the `exportResult` message (or never). If the host never emits `exportResult` (webview disposed, provider error swallowed, prompt never resolves), `exportStatus` stays `"exporting"` and the Export button remains permanently disabled with the spinner stuck. Remove the misleading try/catch and instead rely on the message handler plus a safety timeout that transitions to `"error"` (cleared on success/unmount) so the UI cannot deadlock.

`handleKeydown` is bound only to the overlay div, so Escape only works when focus is inside the dialog/overlay. When the dialog opens without programmatic focus (no autofocus here), focus may remain on the body and the div's keydown never fires, so Escape-to-close silently fails. Prefer a window-level `keydown` listener (as `ChatPanel.svelte` does) registered in the `$effect` cleanup, or explicitly focus the dialog on mount.

The card stops propagation of `keydown`, so keyboard events from any focused element inside the dialog never reach the overlay's `handleKeydown`. Since focus is moved into the overlay (and Tab naturally lands on the buttons inside the card), pressing **Escape while focus is on a button inside the card will not dismiss the tour**, and ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Enter navigation keys likewise won't fire. Either remove this stopPropagation and instead scope key handling, or handle Escape/arrows directly on the card. Note `ExportDialog.svelte` uses the same stopPropagation pattern, but there it is harmless because its overlay only listens for Escape and no inner element relies on bubbling.

When a button inside the card has focus and the user presses Enter, the browser fires a `click` on that button. The `onclick` click then bubbles to the overlay's `onclick={onDismiss}` — but the card already calls `e.stopPropagation()` on click, so that specific bubble is blocked. However, Enter also dispatches `keydown` to the overlay handler via bubbling only if the card did not stop it; more importantly, pressing Enter on the last step triggers `onComplete()` via the overlay handler while the click handler/button may independently invoke `next()`/`onComplete` again. Because `onComplete`/`onDismiss` are not guarded against re-entry, repeated Enter/ArrowRight presses on the last step can invoke the callback multiple times (e.g. double-completing or double-persisting dismiss state). Add a `finished`/`dismissed` guard flag that makes `next()`/`onComplete()`/`onDismiss()` idempotent.

`aria-modal="true"` is set, but `focusOnMount` only focuses the overlay once; there is no focus trap. Tab can move focus out of the dialog to background content behind the overlay, which violates the modal contract for keyboard and screen-reader users. Consider trapping Tab/Shift+Tab within the card (or add an inert/`aria-hidden` on background content while the dialog is open).

The rendered step is clamped via `safeStep`, but the navigation controls, `isLast`, and `prev()`/`next()` all read the raw `step`. `isLast` (`step === steps.length - 1`) drives the primary button label ("✨ Got it!" vs "Next") and the `onComplete` path, so if `step` ever becomes out of range the displayed step and the enabled/disabled controls can disagree (e.g. Back enabled while showing step 0, or Next/`isLast` inconsistent with the shown step). Derive `isLast` from `safeStep` and use `safeStep` consistently for `disabled={safeStep === 0}` and for `next()`/`prev()` bounds so display and controls can never diverge.

comments.content: The regex passed into `renderInline`/`renderMarkdown` is the shared reactive `searchRegex` proxy, not a fresh copy. `String.prototype.replace` with a `/g` regex does reset `lastIndex`, so replace() itself is safe — but this regex also feeds `.test()`/`.exec()` elsewhere and, more importantly, `freshSearchRegex()` was introduced precisely to avoid statefulness. To keep a single source of truth and avoid subtle lastIndex/staleness bugs, pass `freshSearchRegex()` here (or clone inside `renderInline`) rather than the raw reactive proxy.

This `$effect` only reads `markdownRoot` (its reactive dependency), so it runs once when the root element is first bound. Subsequent content updates — streaming tokens, `message.content`/`message.thinking` changes, or tool-result HTML replacing a tool body via `{@html}` — re-render the inner HTML but do NOT re-run this effect. Newly injected `.md-header-anchor` / `.md-fragment-link` nodes therefore never receive click handlers after the first render, so header-copy and fragment-scroll silently break for streamed/updated content. Depend on the rendered content (e.g. read a content-derived signal such as `message.content`/`searchQuery` here, or use a Svelte action/`{@attach}` on the container) so handlers are re-wired after every render.

`navigator.clipboard.writeText()` returns a Promise that can reject (non-secure context, permission denied, transient failure). In both `copyCode` and `copyMessage` the promise is left unhandled while `copiedCode`/`copiedMessage` is optimistically set to `true`, so the UI reports a successful copy even when the write failed and can surface an unhandled promise rejection. Await/handle the promise and only flip the flag on success.

`match.line` is escaped via `escapeHtml`, which is correct for text nodes, but if a grep tool returns `match.line` as a non-string value (e.g. a number or null), `escapeHtml` calls `.replace` on it and throws a TypeError, aborting the whole render. Given `details` is externally supplied tool data, coerce defensively (e.g. `escapeHtml(String(match.line ?? ""))`).

The envelope validation discards array payloads: any `envelope.data` that is an Array is replaced with `{}`. The host sends `provider-auth` with an **array** as the payload (`getProviderAuthData()` returns `Array<...>`), so `data` becomes `{}` and the `Array.isArray(data)` branch below always yields `providers = []` — provider settings will therefore never populate. Preserve arrays when unwrapping the envelope (e.g. `const data = envelope.data ?? {}` and validate per-case), and type the branch against `unknown` so array payloads are not silently dropped.

`editRequestIndex` is set when the host requests an edit but is never reset to `null` after ChatPanel consumes it. ChatPanel re-runs its `$effect` whenever it remounts (e.g. tab switch back to chat) and will re-trigger the edit prompt for a stale index; additionally, if the same index is requested twice in a row, the value does not change so the child effect may not fire at all. Reset it to `null` after dispatching, or use a monotonically increasing tick like `searchRequestTick`.

Several `pi-event` handlers read nested fields without validating their shape (e.g. `event.result?.content?.map(...)`, `event.assistantMessageEvent.delta`, `event.messages[i].role`). A malformed or unexpected event payload from the host can throw inside `handlePiEvent`, which is invoked from the window `message` listener — an uncaught exception there aborts processing of the remaining stream and can leave `isStreaming` stuck true. Guard the `handlePiEvent` call (try/catch) and/or validate `delta`/`content` types before use.

In the fallback partial sync, `content` is only overwritten when the partial is *longer* than the accumulated buffer. When deltas are dropped or the stream reconnects, the accumulated buffer and the authoritative partial can diverge at the same length yet differ in content (duplicate/lost text). Consider comparing with `!==` and preferring the partial when it is at least as long, instead of a strict `>` length check, to avoid persisting corrupted transcripts.

`activeToolCalls` is declared as `$state(new Map())`, but Svelte 5 only makes plain objects/arrays deeply reactive; a native `Map` is not proxied, so `.set()/.delete()/.clear()` do not trigger reactivity. The UI currently re-renders because `messages` is also reassigned, but any future template/derived value reading `activeToolCalls` will not update. Use `SvelteMap` from `svelte/reactivity` (or plain non-reactive `let`) to avoid a subtle latent bug.

comments.content: The hosted `window` message listener does not verify the message origin/source. Any frame or window able to post to this webview can drive `handleVSCodeMessage` (e.g. injecting fake `session-history`, `error`, or `extension-notify` payloads that become rendered chat content / XSS vectors). Validate `event.source === window` (or check `event.origin`) before processing.

`models` is assigned directly from host data without an Array check (`models = data.models`). A malformed payload sets `models` to `undefined`, after which `models.find(...)` in `availableThinkingLevels` and `getModelDisplay` will throw on every render. Guard with `Array.isArray(data.models)`.

Any bare `error` message with no `requestId` while *any* auth check is in flight clears ALL `checkingProvider` flags and shows a single toast. If two providers are checked concurrently (or an unrelated host error arrives), this silently cancels the in-flight state of checks that never received a real result, leaving the UI inconsistent and the disabled buttons re-enabled with no result. Prefer correlating check results by `requestId` (send one with `checkProviderAuth`) and only clear the specific provider's flag, rather than treating every uncorrelated error as an auth-check failure.

`checkAuth` never correlates its request: no `requestId` is sent, so the reply handler must rely on `d.provider`, and the uncorrelated-error path above cannot be attributed to a specific provider. Without an id, a late/duplicate result for provider A can clear state for provider B (or vice versa). Include a per-request id in `checkProviderAuth` and key `authCheckResults`/`checkingProvider` by that id.

`removeAuth` optimistically mutates local `providers` (marks unconfigured) but the host reply is never correlated, so a host-side failure leaves the UI claiming credentials were removed while the backend still holds them. Use a requestId-correlated reply and only update local state once the host confirms success (as `deleteProvider` correctly does).

`saveApiKey` also optimistically flips the provider to configured/"stored" immediately after posting, before the host confirms the key was persisted. If the write fails, the UI shows a bogus success state; there is no error handling at all for this path. Correlate this request and update state only on a confirmed reply.

The correlated `error` branch clears `pendingAddId`/`pendingRequestId` but leaves `fetchingModels`/`pendingFetchId` untouched, and more importantly the success path relies on `resetAddForm()` to clear everything. If the add request fails, `fetchingModels` is not part of this path so no stuck state there — but note the add button is disabled solely on `pendingAddId`; a host that never replies leaves the form permanently stuck. Consider a timeout or clearing pending state in more paths.

Model discovery sends the trimmed API key from the form (`apiKey: newProviderApiKey.trim()`) to the host, while the hint text adjacent claims "stored keys are never sent back to this form". Ensure the host does not log or persist this transient key and that its only use is the /models request; the current hint could mislead users into pasting a key they believe won't leave the form. Also confirm the URL built from `newProviderBaseUrl` is validated host-side to avoid SSRF.

The `{#each}` blocks for both configured and unconfigured providers key on `p.name`. Display names are not guaranteed unique (two custom providers can share a name, or an empty name is possible), producing duplicate keys and wrong DOM reuse. Key on the stable `p.provider` id instead in both lists.

`loginResults` assignment is gated on `if (d.success !== true || d.message)`. A successful result carrying only an `error` field (or neither message nor error) is silently dropped, and an unsuccessful result with no message/error yields a card with an empty body. Store the result unconditionally on failure so the user always sees feedback.

`respondPrompt`/`cancelPrompt` receive `promptId` but never use it in the send payload's `promptId` fallback beyond what the caller passes — the caller uses `login.prompt?.promptId ?? ""`, and by the time this runs the prompt may already be cleared. Sending an empty `promptId` silently would break host-side prompt correlation. Guard against empty promptId before sending.

`JSON.parse` output is assigned directly to `recentTemplates` typed as `Template[]` with no runtime validation. Corrupted/legacy localStorage data can yield non-arrays (e.g. `null`, `{}`, a number) or objects missing `tags`/`category`, which then crash rendering: `{#each template.tags as tag}` throws on undefined tags, and `categoryLabels[template.category]` yields undefined. Validate the parsed shape (array + required string fields) and filter/normalize before assigning.

The `$effect` focuses `searchInput` but has no explicit mount-only guard. Because it reads `searchInput`, any reassignment of that binding re-triggers it; more importantly `$effect` re-runs after DOM updates while this component is mounted, which can repeatedly steal focus back to the search box (e.g. after user tabs to a template button or the close button). Consider using `onMount(() => searchInput?.focus())` or an `$effect` that runs once, so focus is not captured on every update.

Escape-to-close is bound as `onkeydown` on the overlay div, which only fires when that element (or a descendant) has focus. `tabindex="-1"` makes it focusable but nothing focuses it on mount (only the search input is focused), so keydown events target the input and bubble to the overlay — acceptable while focus stays inside the dialog, but once focus moves outside the dialog subtree Escape silently stops closing the modal. Bind the listener globally (e.g. `svelte:window onkeydown`) to make dismissal reliable.

`onClose` is invoked both here in `useTemplate` and again in the parent `handleInsertPromptTemplate` (which sets `showPromptTemplates = false`). This double-close is redundant and makes the component's contract ambiguous (it closes itself even though the caller also closes it). Remove one of the two so ownership of dismissal is clear.

Search navigation index and auto-scroll can desync from the highlighted match. `currentMatchIndex` is used as `scrollToMatch(msgIndex)` and to set `.search-current`; when `messages.length <= visibleMessageCount` its value is a *global* index, but when more messages exist than the rendered window, `scrollToMatch` receives an index that may be `>=` the requested window size — the function then rewrites `visibleMessageCount` to `messages.length - msgIndex + 10`, permanently growing the rendered slice instead of raising a "show more" prompt, and later `goToNextMatch` reads back a mismatched `currentSearchIdx`. Also `scrollToMatch` is `async` and is called without awaiting from `goToNextMatch`/`goToPrevMatch` (and from the typing effect), so concurrent ticks can interleave `visibleMessageCount`/`scrollTop` writes. Consider deriving indices consistently against the full `messages` array and guarding re-entrancy of the scroll routine.

`transition` prop names may be inconsistent between call sites: this passes `onToggle`, and `ContextIndicator` expects `onCompact`. Verify each component's declared props match what ChatPanel passes (e.g. `ResourceBadge` uses `previousCount` and `count`, `VoiceCapture` accepts `onToggle`). A mismatch silently drops the handler in Svelte 5 runes mode, disabling voice/compact actions without an error.

Unbounded image accumulation with no size/type validation. `readImageFile` accepts any `image/*` file and pushes it into `inputImages` without checking a byte limit or a max count, and `handleDrop` loops over all dropped files doing the same. A user dropping many large images (or a single huge one) will read the entire file as base64 into memory and later send an oversized payload to the extension host. Add per-file size and total-count limits and reject unsupported mime types before reading.

Prefer a functional/`push`-style update and add `reader.onerror` so a failed read does not silently drop the attachment.

The window-level Ctrl+F handler duplicates the panel-level (`handleGlobalKeydown`) and textarea-level (`handleKeydown`) Ctrl+F handling. Because the window listener runs during the bubble phase after the inner handlers already called `preventDefault`, the `e.defaultPrevented` guard covers most cases, but the F3 branch here has no `defaultPrevented` check and no `e.target === searchInputEl` short-circuit, so an F3 keypress inside the search input can be handled twice (once here, once by `handleSearchInputKeydown`), double-advancing the match. Gate F3 on `!e.defaultPrevented` and skip when the target is the search input.

The `searchRequestTick`/`focusInputRequestTick` effects fire on any non-zero value including unchanged re-runs. Since they only compare `> 0`, if these props are reset to 0 and then set again to the same tick they will still fire, which is intended, but re-running on unrelated reactive reads is a risk if `openSearch`/`focusChatInput` later reads tracked state. More importantly, `openSearch()` calls `tick().then(...)` without cleanup, so a component unmount before the microtask resolves will focus a detached element. Consider returning a cancellation/`mounted` guard. (Low severity, verify against the prop contract.)

`handleKeydown` checks `e.key === "Enter"` and submits before the Escape/arrow-key branches below, but the ordering means an Enter pressed while the @ autocomplete is open when `filteredFiles.length === 0` falls through to `handleSubmit()`, sending the literal `@query` text as a message. Also `applySlashCommand`/`selectFile` are only invoked when their filtered lists are non-empty; when empty the Enter path should be swallowed rather than sent. Add an early return when an autocomplete trigger is active regardless of list length.

The keydown handler advances `selectedIndex`/`selectedSlashIndex` with `Math.min/Math.max` against the *filtered* list length, but when the filtered length shrinks below the current index (e.g. the user keeps typing and the query narrows), the stale index can point past the end of the list. The array access `filteredSlashCommands[selectedSlashIndex]` in Enter/Tab then yields `undefined` and `applySlashCommand(undefined)` throws. Clamp the index whenever `filteredSlashCommands`/`filteredFiles` change (e.g. in a derived or an effect) instead of only on key events.

`addPathToInput` computes the cursor-following position as `textBeforeCursor.length + path.length + 2`, but when an `@token` was present it takes the first branch (line replacing via match) and skips the `requestAnimationFrame`/`setSelectionRange`, so the caret is left wherever it was — the comment/logic implies the caret should move after the inserted path. Ensure both branches reposition the caret consistently (as `selectFile` does via `setTimeout(focus)`).

The auto-scroll effect writes `el.scrollTop = el.scrollHeight` while the container has `scroll-behavior: smooth`, inside the same effect that also writes `showScrollBtn`. Because it reads `el.scrollHeight`/`scrollTop`/`clientHeight` (layout) and writes state, this effect will re-run on every `messages` update and can fight the search scroll (`scrollToMatch`) and the user's manual scroll during streaming, producing jitter. Reading layout in an effect that also mutates DOM scroll is a known anti-pattern here; consider driving scroll from an explicit "new message" signal rather than tracking raw layout values.

`isInstalled` infers install state from a case-insensitive substring test, so a package named `foo` reports "Installed" when only `foo-bar`, `@scope/foo-extra`, or an unrelated `npm:.../foo...` source is present — and conversely the real package can be missed. It also does not normalize scoped names, so `@scope/pkg` vs `pkg` mismatch. Compare the exact source key instead (e.g. `p.source === 'npm:' + name` and, for scoped names, a suffix match on `/name`), rather than `includes`.

Worse, if the host's `loading: false` later arrives, it will call `refreshInstalled()` and the modal has already been closed — the user loses the "operation still running" indication while the package manager may still be mutating state. `togglePackage` and the rendering of enable/disable state only look at client-side `disabledPackages`, which is populated from the host `resource-toggles-changed` payload (shape-checked for strings only). The initial `getResourceToggles` response is never handled here, so before that event arrives the UI assumes every package is enabled and can send `enabled: false` for an already-disabled package; conversely the host enforces config. Verify the sender/origin (or a nonce) before trusting this payload, or restrict the state source to the awaited response.

The `installed` message handling validates only that `source` is a string; the code then dereferences `pkg.source.toLowerCase()` (via `isPackageEnabled`/`displayPackageName`) for every rendered entry, and `pkg.types`/`pkg.skills`/etc. are used as arrays in the template. A host/forged payload with `source: null` or missing `types` can throw during render and break the panel. Normalize each entry (default `types`/`skills`/`extensions`/`prompts` to `[]`, coerce string fields) when assigning `installedPackages`.

`applyBatchTypes` fans out up to 20 unauthenticated requests to registry.npmjs.org per batch with no timeout, no concurrency limit across the whole run, and no `AbortController`. Also `applyBatchTypes` unconditionally runs `marketplacePackages = [...marketplacePackages]` even after the caller detected a stale sequence (the `return` happens before this in most paths, but the final batch's copy still re-triggers reactivity on the whole list per batch, i.e. O(n) copies). Consider aborting superseded fetches and only bumping reactivity once per batch for the current sequence.

Use the anchor `rel`/target as in the installed-tab link, or pass `'noopener,noreferrer'` to `window.open`.

`installPackage`, `removePackage`, `updatePackages` and `refreshInstalled` are declared `async` but never await anything; the returned promises are also dropped at call sites (e.g. `onclick={fetchMarketplacePackages}` on the refresh button). This is misleading and hides rejected promises. Drop `async` where there is no await, and wrap the refresh click handler so a rejection is not silently unhandled.

comments.content: `isListening` is destructured from `$props()` and then reassigned inside the message handler. In Svelte 5, props obtained via `$props()` are read-only at the binding site; writing to them is unsupported and will not propagate to the parent (`ChatPanel` owns `isListening` and passes it down). This either triggers a dev-mode ownership warning or silently desyncs the button from the real dictation state. The listening state should be lifted to the parent (e.g. emit an event/callback that lets `ChatPanel` update its own state), or the message handler should live in the parent where the state is owned.

The `$effect` reads `isListening` (via the enclosing scope reference inside `handleVSCodeMessage`), so any change to listening state re-runs the effect: the old `window` "message" listener is removed and a new one added. This produces listener churn and, more importantly, a window where no listener is attached, so a `voice-listening-changed` event emitted during that gap is silently dropped. The handler does not need the current `isListening` value to dispatch its work; restructure so only `isListening`'s update path is reactive without re-subscribing the listener (e.g. keep the listener subscription independent of state, or subscribe once in `onMount`).

Only the message shape is validated (via `parseHostMessage`); there is no check on `event.origin` or `event.source`. Any script, iframe, or injected frame that can post a well-formed `{type: "voice-listening-changed", data: {listening: true}}` message to this window can flip the dictation state. Validate that the event originates from the expected VS Code origin/source before trusting it.

`parseHostMessage` returns `null` for any unexpected envelope, and the message is dropped with no logging or fallback. If the extension host ever emits a legitimate payload that does not match the expected shape (e.g. a future envelope change), the button silently desyncs from the actual dictation state with no diagnostic. Consider reporting/surfacing parse failures so such desyncs are detectable.

`duration` is not validated. `Infinity` isn't practically reachable here, but `NaN` is: `duration > 0` is `false` for `NaN`, so a caller passing `duration: Number(badInput)` silently produces a toast that never auto-dismisses (same as `persistent`) instead of failing fast. Consider normalizing: treat non-finite / non-positive durations as "no auto-dismiss" explicitly, or coerce and log. Also note `persistent` combined with an explicit `duration` ignores the duration — document/validate that precedence to avoid caller confusion.

Eviction drops the oldest toast via `dismissToast`, but this runs *after* the new toast has already been pushed, and the surrounding `toasts` mutation is a plain array assignment rather than a reactive-safe update. More importantly, the module-level `timers` Map is never released when the host component unmounts. If Toast.svelte is destroyed/re-mounted (HMR, conditional render) without `clearToasts()` being called, pending timeouts keep firing against module state whose $state was discarded, and the Map grows monotonically. Add an `$effect`/`onDestroy` cleanup that calls `clearToasts()` (and nulls `window.__toast`) when the component is torn down.

The global assignment is unconditional, so a second mount (or HMR re-execution of the module under Vite, where the module scope is re-evaluated while the page persists) overwrites the previous instance's `window.__toast`. Any timers registered against the old Map become orphaned — they still fire, call the old `dismissToast`, and can never be cleared because the old instance is no longer reachable through `window.__toast`. Guard against clobbering (e.g. `if (!window.__toast) { ... }` or reuse an existing instance) and rely on the `Window.__toast` declaration in `app.d.ts` instead of the `any` cast to retain type safety.

The container announces politely (`role="status"` + `aria-live="polite"`) while each individual toast is `role="alert"` (assertive). Nesting assertive live regions inside a polite one produces inconsistent/double announcements across screen readers. Pick one strategy: either keep the container live region and use plain `role="group"`/no role on the toast, or drop the container live region and let each `role="alert"` toast announce itself. As written the inner `role="alert"` on an element that is generated via animation is also announced on insertion regardless of the container settings.

The static `style="animation: toast-in ..."` is redundant: the `.toast` CSS class below already sets the same `animation` declaration. Removing the inline style avoids maintainability drift where the two values diverge (and it also duplicates the animation onto the same element, which some engines will treat as an unnecessary style attribute).

A negative, fractional, `NaN`, or `Infinity` count produces unexpected results (e.g. `Array(-1)` throws at runtime, `Array(2.5)` throws a RangeError, and `Array(Infinity)` / a huge value can hang or exhaust memory) since the value is used directly as the iteration length. Clamp/validate the prop before building the array.

comments.content: `event.data` is treated as trusted here: it is destructured directly (`const { type } = event.data`) and `event.data.data` is accessed without shape validation. The window `message` listener receives messages dispatched by ANY origin/window, and the sibling App.svelte handler explicitly guards this (`if (!raw || typeof raw !== "object") return;`) because a non-object payload throws on destructuring. A `null`/non-object `event.data` would throw a TypeError here, and an unexpected `String`/`Array` payload for `event.data.data` is then compared as if it were an event object. Add the same envelope guard used elsewhere before reading `type`/`data` (and prefer `event.origin`/`event.source` checks).

The streaming flag is only ever set by `message_start`/`tool_execution_start` and cleared by `message_end`/`tool_execution_end`/`agent_end`. The provider's event stream (AgentSessionEvent) can terminate a turn without a matching ending event ever reaching the webview — e.g. an error/abort path, an event dropped while the webview was hidden/reloaded, or `agent_end` not firing. In those cases `isStreaming` stays `true` and the spinner (and its interval) runs forever. Verify the event contract guarantees a terminal event, and add a fallback (e.g. clear on session reset / a timeout).

The interval callback reads and writes `spinnerIndex`, which is `$state`. Because `spinnerIndex` is read inside the effect's (asynchronous) interval callback, it is not a tracked dependency of this `$effect`, so no self-retrigger occurs — but this is fragile and easy to break. More importantly, the accumulator pattern means every interval tick creates a new reactive write. Use an updater that doesn't read the tracked value across the async boundary (e.g. `spinnerIndex = (spinnerIndex + 1) % ...` is fine only by relying on untracked async reads); a safer form is to compute the next index from a local counter or wrap the read in `untrack`.

`extensionStatusLine` recomputes `Object.entries(...).filter(...).sort(...).map(...)` over the whole `activities` map on every change. `$derived` caches, but if `activities` is reassigned on every streamed event (e.g. each tool_start/end), this full sort+map runs at high frequency during streaming. If activity maps can grow large, consider memoizing per-item sanitization or sorting keys only when the key set changes.

`sanitizeStatusText` assumes `item.text` is a string; if an activity item ever carries a non-string `text` (untyped upstream data), `.replace` throws inside the derived and breaks rendering. Guard the input (`typeof text === "string" ? text : ""`) since `ActivityItem` is only a compile-time interface over runtime data.

Consider reconciling once (e.g. call `onThinkingLevelChange(effectiveThinkingLevel)` inside an `$effect` when `thinkingLevel !== effectiveThinkingLevel`, being careful to avoid a feedback loop).

`onShowCacheMissNoticesChange` / `onLightModeChange` are optional (guarded before invoking), yet the corresponding toggles are always rendered and enabled. When the callback is undefined the checkbox still visually flips on click while nothing is persisted, leaving the control out of sync with the props. Either disable/hide the toggle when the handler is absent (like the Auto Context toggle does with `disabled`), or render the switch in a read-only state.

The `$effect` has no reactive dependencies, so it registers exactly once — good. But if `getVsCodeApi()` returns `null` (neither `window.vscode` nor `acquireVsCodeApi` is available yet at mount), the effect bails out permanently and the overrides warning never loads. Additionally, caching the api on `window.vscode` here can race with `App.svelte`, which calls `acquireVsCodeApi()` unconditionally; VS Code's `acquireVsCodeApi` is intended to be called only once per webview. Prefer centralizing acquisition in `App.svelte` and reading the already-cached `window.vscode`, or at minimum tolerate the null case without silently dropping the request.

`height` and `width` are string props interpolated verbatim into an inline `style` attribute. Nothing prevents a caller from passing a value containing `;` and additional declarations (e.g. `"100px; background: url(...)"`), which permits style injection. Validate/sanitize the values (e.g. restrict to a safe length/units regex, or use CSS custom properties) before interpolating.

The fallback logic `height || width || '32px'` and `width || '32px'` is inconsistent: an explicit empty string (or `0` passed as a number) is treated as absent, and for `circle`/`bar` the default `height`/`width` may be `'auto'` from the Props default, yielding `height: auto; width: auto` on a zero-content element so the placeholder collapses and becomes invisible. Use explicit `undefined` checks (`height ?? width ?? '32px'`) and guard against non-size values like `'auto'` for these shapes.

The duplication is a divergence hazard (e.g. the `text` branch uses its own sizing rules rather than the shared ones). comments.content: `deleteSelectedSessions` clears the local selection but never re-requests the session list. The host does not push a `sessions-list` after deletion (message-handler only sends it in response to an explicit `listSessions`/`session-updated`), so the deleted rows stay visible and the user must manually trigger a refresh. Re-request the list after issuing the delete so the UI reflects the host state.

The single-session delete path has the same refresh gap: after `deleteSession` the deleted session remains in `sessions` because the host never pushes an updated list. Also `selectedNodeId`/`activeSessionId` are not reset, so the panel may keep highlighting a row that no longer exists. Re-fetch the list and clear the local pointers.

This cleanup effect only clears `selectedSessionIds` when a list is present and selection mode is off, so it never reconciles the selection against the current session list. After a refresh/delete, ids that no longer exist are retained in the SvelteSet, inflating the "N selected" count and being sent back in the `deleteSessions` payload. Prune the set to only ids still present in `sessions` whenever the list changes.

In selection mode, selecting a session does not update `selectedNodeId`, so the keyboard navigation state and the `aria-activedescendant` attribute stay stale. More importantly, `Enter` is handled both here (panel-level) and by each row's own `onkeydown`, so a single Enter on a focused row can invoke `selectSession`/`toggleSessionSelection` twice. Guard against duplicate handling and keep `selectedNodeId` in sync with clicks.

Make the empty-list case explicit to avoid relying on the guard.

`formatTime` computes elapsed time from `Date.now()` but there is no reactive timer, so relative labels ("Just now", "5m ago") never re-render as time passes and remain stale until an unrelated state change forces a re-render. Consider a periodic tick or absolute timestamps.

With an active search filter, "Select all" selects sessions the user cannot see, and the subsequent "Delete selected" would delete hidden sessions. Index desync: `builtinTools` is a derived/filtered subset, so `index` from `{#each builtinTools as tool, index}` is an index into the filtered list, not into `tools`. `toggleTool(index)` indexes the full `tools` array. comments.content: `start()` captures the passed `session` in the interval closure. If a session value can change while polling continues, the poller will keep reporting stale data from the originally captured session; if session is null/undefined the interval still runs but sendFooterData silently returns every tick, needlessly consuming a timer. Consider holding the session as an instance field (e.g. `private session`) that can be updated via start/stop, so the poller always reads the current one, and don't schedule the interval when session is nullish.

`resolveGitBranch` is a synchronous call executed on every 5s tick with no error handling. If it throws, the exception escapes the interval callback. While Node's setInterval will keep rescheduling after a thrown callback, the exception surfaces as an uncaught error and all subsequent footer updates for that tick are lost. Wrap the call (or the whole sendFooterData body) in try/catch and log/surface failures so a single bad branch resolution doesn't disrupt footer updates.
The 5000 ms poll interval is a hardcoded magic number. Extract it into a named constant (e.g. `POLL_INTERVAL_MS`) for readability and to avoid magic-number drift.

`diagnosticsBuffer` grows unbounded: every `logDiagnostics` call appends lines and nothing ever trims it. The buffer is also exported in full via `getDiagnosticsLogContent()`. In a long-running session with diagnostics enabled (e.g. the periodic update checker calls `logDiagnostics` repeatedly), this leaks memory and can produce very large exports. Consider a size cap with FIFO eviction (e.g. keep the last N lines/bytes).

`typeof arg === "string" ? arg : JSON.stringify(arg, null, 2)` — `JSON.stringify` throws on circular references (and on BigInt), and the arguments passed by callers include arbitrary objects/errors (e.g. `logDiagnostics(..., err)`). A throw here would propagate into the logging call site and may break unrelated code paths. Wrap serialization in a try/catch (or use a safe stringifier) and fall back to `String(arg)`.

comments.content: `setDiagnosticsEnabled(false)` stops logging but leaves the accumulated `diagnosticsBuffer` intact, whereas the only way to clear it is the test-only `resetDiagnosticsStateForTests` (guarded by PI_TEST). Consequently, an export performed after disabling diagnostics still contains stale entries, and users have no way to clear the log. Consider clearing the buffer when diagnostics are disabled (or exposing a public reset), so exported content reflects the current session.

Hardcoded 500ms delay after focusSidebar is a fragile race: if the webview/panel isn't ready within 500ms the prompt may be sent before the chat view can receive it, and the delay also blocks the command unnecessarily. Consider awaiting an explicit readiness signal (e.g., a webview 'ready' handshake) instead of a fixed sleep.

This refactorCode handler repeats the same focus+fixed-delay pattern; the 500ms sleep is again a race against panel readiness. Extract a shared helper (e.g., focusSidebarAndWaitReady) and replace the fixed delay with a readiness handshake to keep behavior consistent across commands.

analyzeProject silently proceeds with an empty folderPath when neither the uri nor workspaceFolders is available, producing a prompt like 'Analyze the project at ``'. Guard for a missing path and show a warning instead.

Most command handlers (explainCode, refactorCode, analyzeProject, navigateToSession, cycleModel, cycleThinkingLevel, toggleVoiceCapture, install/remove/update resources, openCurrentSessionInEditor, newChatInEditor, rebuildNativeAddons, etc.) await provider calls without try/catch, so failures become unhandled promise rejections with no user-facing feedback. This is inconsistent with generateCommitMessage/exportDiagnosticsLog which do handle errors. Wrap these handlers in try/catch and surface vscode.window.showErrorMessage.

deleteSessions. await provider.deleteSessions(sessionIds) is not wrapped in try/catch, so a failure here is an unhandled rejection; the success message is also shown unconditionally even if deletion partially fails. Wrap the call and only report success on completion, showing an error otherwise.

Destructive irreversible delete uses a modal with buttons ordered ["Cancel", "Delete"]; making the destructive action the non-default (right-hand/affirmative) button while Cancel is listed first helps prevent accidental confirmation. Confirm the ordering/default matches VS Code conventions for destructive modals.

The diagnostics config listener keys off 'pi-agent.diagnostics' but the read config path is 'diagnostics.enabled'. Depending on VS Code's key-prefix matching, this may be intended, but the mismatch is confusing and fragile. Use the exact key 'pi-agent.diagnostics.enabled' in affectsConfiguration to guarantee the toggle reacts to the actual setting.

`resolveAtStartup` sets `pathResolved = true` even when the binary is not found (`resolvedBinaryPath` stays null). Because of this, a later valid resolution (e.g. after the user installs `pi` or fixes `pi-agent.binaryPath`) will never re-resolve via this method, and the service permanently reports `isBinaryAvailable() === false`. The failure state should not be cached, or a re-resolve/reload path should be provided.

`restorePath` is dead code: it is only referenced by unit tests and never called from production code (see pi-agent-provider.ts which calls `prependToPath()` but never restores). Since `prependToPath` mutates the global `process.env.PATH`, the absence of a paired restore means the injected `binaryDir` leaks into the whole extension host for the session lifetime. Either wire up restore after the spawn completes, or document why the leak is acceptable.

`getCliVersion` swallows every error with an empty catch and returns `null` without any logging, contradicting the comment "logging handled by caller" (callers such as `pi-agent-provider.ts` do not log the failure either). A silent per-invocation failure (e.g. binary not executable) will be hard to diagnose. Log the failure via `this.deps.logError`/`logDebug` before returning null.

`getCliVersion` mixes `stdout` and `stderr` into the cached version string. If the binary prints warnings to stderr alongside the real version on stdout, or vice-versa, the cached value becomes an arbitrary concatenation and downstream version parsing/comparison will silently produce wrong results. Fall back to stderr only when stdout is empty, and validate the trimmed output looks like a version.

The three accessors return values from different lookup strategies: `getResolvedPath()` returns the cached `resolvedBinaryPath` (null until `resolveAtStartup` runs), `resolveBinary()` re-runs `resolvePiBinary()`, and `getBinaryPath()` returns `findPiBinary()` (which can return a bare `"pi"` non-absolute name). These can diverge — e.g. `pi-agent-provider.ts` line 3225 uses `getResolvedPath() ?? getBinaryPath()`, so it can fall back to a non-absolute `"pi"` while `resolveBinary()` would have returned the real absolute path. Consolidate on a single source of truth to avoid confusing/inconsistent results.

The `.git`/HEAD parsing relies on hardcoded magic offsets `slice(16)` and `slice(8)` matching the literal prefixes. These are brittle and would silently misparse if the prefixes ever change. Consider extracting the prefix stripping into named constants or a small helper so the offset and the prefix string are kept in sync (the duplication between the directory and `gitdir:` branches also invites drift).

When a `.git` file contains a `gitdir:` pointer but the resolved `HEAD` file does not exist, the code returns `null` immediately instead of continuing the upward walk. This aborts branch detection even if an ancestor directory is a valid repo (e.g. a submodule/worktree with a stale or temporarily missing gitdir). Also, a malformed `.git` file lacking the `gitdir: ` prefix falls through to the parent directory rather than reporting anything, which can mask corruption. Confirm the intended behavior for these edge cases.

`resolveGitBranch` performs synchronous filesystem calls (`existsSync`/`statSync`/`readFileSync`) while walking parent directories and is invoked during command execution. This blocks the extension host event loop. Consider an async variant (`fs.promises`) or caching the result, especially since the same workspace is queried repeatedly.

The case-insensitive normalization is gated on `process.platform === "win32"`, but `findRepositoryRoot()` derives `repoRoot` from `path.resolve(cwd)` while `repository.rootUri.fsPath` comes from the git extension's own resolution. On macOS the default APFS/HFS+ volume is also case-insensitive, and the two paths can differ in case (e.g. `/Users/Me/repo` vs `/users/me/repo`), so the exact-string comparison fails and the lookup falsely returns `unavailable`, silently dropping the commit message. Consider comparing canonicalized paths (e.g. `fs.realpathSync`) or applying case-folding on all case-insensitive platforms rather than only win32.

comments.content: Path comparison is a raw string equality after the optional case-fold; it does not account for trailing path separators or symlinked roots. `repoRoot` is a resolved path from `path.resolve` while `rootUri.fsPath` may retain a trailing separator or resolve through a symlink, so a legitimate match can be reported as `unavailable`. Normalizing both sides (strip trailing separators and/or resolve via `realpath`) before comparing would make the match robust.

`writeCommitMessage` overwrites `inputBox.value` unconditionally, so any commit message the user already typed is silently discarded. The doc comment only claims fill-only semantics (no staging/commit), but clobbering existing user input is still a data-loss side effect. Consider guarding on an empty existing value or preserving/appending the prior message, and documenting the overwrite behavior explicitly.

The provider config snapshot mapping (defaultModel/defaultProvider/autoContext/maxTokens/thinkingLevel/sessionDir) is duplicated verbatim between `activate` and `installConfigListener`. When a default or key changes, one copy will drift from the other, causing the activation-time config and the change-time config to diverge silently. Extract a single helper (e.g. `readProviderConfig(): PiAgentConfig`) and call it from both sites.

The rebuild decision only consults three keys and it also checks the same keys again via the `pi-agent.` prefix. `resourceConfigKeys` already contains `disabledSkills` and `disabledPackages`, but those are handled in the rebuild branch, so the array membership check is effectively dead for them. More importantly this works only by ordering: any new resource-affecting key added to `resourceConfigKeys` will silently take the reload path even though loader construction-time options require a rebuild. Consider making the rebuild-triggering keys a single explicit set disjoint from `resourceConfigKeys` to avoid the overlap/duplication.

Config-change handlers are fire-and-forget: `restartSessionPreservingHistory` / `reloadSessionResources` rejections are only logged via `logDebug`, so a failure leaves the user with a stale/blank webview and no visible feedback. Surface the failure (e.g. `vscode.window.showErrorMessage` or provider status) in addition to the debug log. Note also `reloadSessionResources` already logs errors internally and swallows them (returns a resolved promise), so the `.catch` here is effectively unreachable for that path.

`newSession()` is called when `!provider.hasSession`. But `resolveWebviewView` already creates a session on first view resolve, and focusing the view (`piAgentChat.focus`) may trigger that asynchronous initialization. If the panel is still initializing (or between teardown and create), `hasSession` can be false and this branch will start a second session concurrently with the resolve path, or create a brand-new empty session instead of leaving the existing one—leaving a race that can drop the intended session/discard the user's expectation of continuing. Awaiting provider readiness or relying on the provider's own guarded creation would be safer.

The comment above `resourceConfigKeys` claims "Everything that rewrites loader construction-time options — light mode's `no*` flags — needs a full session rebuild instead," but the array itself contains `disabledSkills`/`disabledPackages`, which are treated as rebuild triggers in the listener. The comment/array are inconsistent about which keys require a rebuild; clarify the split so future keys are categorized correctly.

`Date.parse` returns `NaN` for an unparseable string, and `timestamp ?? 0` only guards against `null`/`undefined` — `NaN` passes through unchanged. An invalid timestamp string therefore emits a `NaN` timestamp to the webview. Guard with `Number.isNaN` (or `Number.isFinite`) before falling back to 0.

The user branch iterates `msg.content` without the element guards used in `extractTextAndImages` (no `if (!c || typeof c !== "object") continue;`) and only tests property *presence* (`"text" in c`, `"data" in c`) rather than `typeof === "string"`. A `null`/primitive element would throw on `c.type`, and a malformed block can push non-string values into `text`/`data`/`mimeType`, defeating the shape-checking the module explicitly claims to do. Reuse `extractTextAndImages` here to keep validation consistent.

The `toolResult` branch maps over `msg.content` and dereferences `c.type`/`c.text` without first checking that `c` is a non-null object (unlike `extractTextAndImages`). A `null`/primitive element injected by an extension would throw a TypeError here and abort the whole serialization pass. Reuse `extractTextAndImages` (or add the `!c || typeof c !== "object"` guard) for consistent defensive handling.

`cliModelIdsCache`/`cliModelIdsPromise` retain a successful-but-empty result for the whole session. When the CLI is temporarily unavailable (or `pi --list-models` transiently fails), `resolveCliModelIds` logs the error and resolves to an empty Set, which is then memoized. Every subsequent `syncFavoritesToSettings`/`syncFromCliModels` call short-circuits on `cliModels.size === 0` and silently no-ops until `invalidateCliModelIdsCache()` is manually invoked, so favorites sync is permanently dead. Consider not caching a rejected/empty resolution (clear `cliModelIdsPromise` so the next call retries) and tracking the failure separately from a legitimate empty list.

`syncFavoritesToSettings` filters `favoriteModels` down to the CLI-known set and writes only those patterns via `setEnabledModels`, but never updates `favoriteModels` or global state. The in-memory/extension favorites can therefore diverge from settings.json (e.g. right after adding a favorite that the CLI does not yet recognize, then re-running sync). Confirm whether the CLI file is meant to be authoritative; if not, favorites unknown to the CLI will be silently dropped from settings.json while still shown in the extension. At minimum reconcile the two lists or document this deliberate asymmetry.

The header filter only excludes a first token exactly equal to `provider` and lines whose raw text starts with `Warning`, which is locale/format dependent and unlikely to match all CLI diagnostic output (progress text, `Error:`/`Info:`/localized warnings, ANSI color codes, etc.). Such lines can inject bogus `provider/model` IDs into the set that is then written to settings.json. Prefer anchoring the whole line (e.g. `/^([^\s]+)\s+([^\s]+)\s+(\S+\s+\S+\s+\S+\s+\S+)\s*$/`) and stripping ANSI/known prefixes before parsing.

When the current model is not in `availableModels`, `currentIndex` is `-1`, so `(0) % models.length === 0` and cycling always jumps to the first model regardless of the previous position — slightly inconsistent with the documented intent. Guard the `-1` case explicitly.

If flush rejects (I/O error, concurrent write), the rejection propagates out of `toggleFavorite` after `favoriteModels`/global state were already updated, leaving global state and settings.json inconsistent and surfacing an unhandled rejection to the caller. Wrap the sync in a try/catch (or `Promise.allSettled`-style handling) with an error log so a settings-sync failure does not fail the whole toggle.

comments.content: `getEnabledModels()` is typed as returning a mutable array and is only used for membership checks; `settingsManager?.getEnabledModels()` is not awaited. If `getEnabledModels` can return a promise or `undefined`, the `|| []` fallback may not cover it — verify the SDK contract. Also consider using a `Set` for the `favoriteModels.includes(...)` / `availableModels.some(...)` lookups when lists grow.

Missing null check on `message.data` for these cases. Calls like `this.provider.prompt(message.data.text, message.data.images)`, `setModel(message.data.modelId)`, `setSessionName(message.data.name)`, `steer(message.data.text)`, `followUp(message.data.text)`, `setThinkingLevel(message.data.level)`, `switchSession(message.data.sessionId)`, and `navigateTree(message.data.nodeId)` dereference `message.data` (and its properties) directly. If the webview sends the message without a `data` payload, this throws a raw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'text')` instead of returning a clean validation error. Other cases in this same switch (e.g. `loginProvider`, `setCommitMessageModel`) guard with `message.data?.x`, so the handling is inconsistent.

`withErrorReporting` already posts an `error` message to the webview and re-throws. Every call site here that passes `message.id` (e.g. `addProvider`, `removeProvider`, `fetchProviderModels`, `openConfigFile`) will therefore emit TWO messages for one failure: the `error` post from `withErrorReporting`, then the `sendResponse(id, errorResult, true)` from the outer catch. On the webview side this can surface duplicate error toasts. Consider using a single error-reporting path (either correlate via `requestId` in `withErrorReporting` or drop the redundant post there).

Fragment extraction does not verify that `session.resourceLoader` actually exposes all four methods. `rl.getSkills()`, `rl.getExtensions()`, and `rl.getPrompts()` are called without optional chaining, while `getAgentsFiles` is guarded with `?.`. If the SDK version loaded lacks any of the unguarded methods, this throws inside the inner `try`, silently swallowing the error and returning empty arrays for all four categories. The guard is inconsistent; apply `?.` consistently (as done for `getAgentsFiles`).

The `navigateTree` case awaits `this.provider.navigateTree(message.data.nodeId)` without `withErrorReporting`, unlike the sibling cases (`switchSession`, `setSessionName`, `steer`, etc.). An error here propagates to the outer catch which only sends a generic `sendResponse`, skipping the webview `error` notification that `withErrorReporting` provides. Wrap it for consistent error handling and also null-check `message.data?.nodeId`.

`toggleFavorite`, `setSkillDiscovery`, `setAutoCompaction`, `setAutoContext`, `setSkillEnabled`, `setPackageEnabled`, `setExtraSkillPaths`, `setApiKey`, and `removeAuth` all dereference `message.data.<prop>` without validation and without `withErrorReporting`. A malformed message throws a raw TypeError that reaches the outer catch and is returned as an opaque error. More importantly, `setSkillEnabled(message.data.key, message.data.enabled)` and similar will silently pass `undefined` through if the property is merely absent, potentially persisting invalid config. Add validation for the presence/type of the payload.

The backdrop of this `deleteSessions` case validates neither the element types nor the array shape: `message.data?.sessionIds ?? []` may be a non-array (e.g. a string) from an untrusted webview message, in which case `.length` and the later `deleteSessions(sessionIds)` receive a string and could iterate characters, deleting wrong sessions or corrupting state. Add `Array.isArray(sessionIds)` validation and ensure each element is a string.

The `preview-diff` temp-file cleanup uses `setTimeout` with a 5-second delay and then deletes the file the diff view is still referencing. If the diff editor takes longer to open (slow machine, large file), the temp file may be removed before VS Code reads it, producing a "file not found" diff or a broken comparison. Also, `fs.unlinkSync`/`readdirSync`/`rmdirSync` silently swallow all errors, hiding real cleanup failures (and leaking temp files). Consider `vscode.workspace.fs.delete` tied to the diff editor lifecycle or shipping the content via a `TextDocumentContentProvider` instead of real temp files.

`openExternalUrl(url)` is guarded here with `/^https?:\/\//i.test(url)`, which is good, but the analogous webview-provided `url` is the only thing checked. Note that the regex allows any http(s) host including internal/metadata endpoints and does not reject URL credentials (e.g. `https://user:pass@host`). Since this ultimately opens the system browser, consider restricting to expected auth hosts or at least documenting why arbitrary hosts are acceptable.

Prefer strict equality per the project's review rules. `message.data.index` and other numeric inputs are passed through without `typeof` validation; combined with the earlier null-check gaps this makes the handler brittle. Also `confirmBtn !== "Delete"` is fine, but the surrounding new code should consistently validate payload shapes.

`getProjectContext` has an unused variable in the try block: `root` is computed but only used in the catch return, while inside the try it returns `root` too — that part is used. However, `name: pkg.name || "Unknown", version: pkg.version || "Unknown"` risks `pkg` being a non-object (e.g. package.json containing `null`), causing a TypeError that silently falls back to the catch branch and reports "Unknown" for a valid workspace. Validate `pkg` is a non-null object after `JSON.parse`.

comments.content: Shell injection risk: `source` (user-supplied) is passed straight into `spawn(binaryPath, args, { shell: true })` on the PATH-resolution branch. Node joins command + args into a single shell line without escaping, so characters such as `;`, `&&`, `|`, `$(...)`, `%VAR%` or embedded quotes in a package source are interpreted by the shell instead of being treated as a literal argument. The `!path.isAbsolute(binaryPath)` condition is also true for any relative/odd path, widening the exposure. Quote the args (the repo already exposes `quoteShellArg`/`getShellCommand` for this) or avoid `shell: true` and pass argv directly.

`output` accumulates the entire stdout+stderr of the spawned command without any bound and is then used verbatim as the rejection message. Verbose commands (e.g. `update`) can consume unbounded memory and produce an enormous error payload pushed to the UI. Cap the retained buffer (e.g. keep only the last N KB for the error message) while still streaming chunks to the webview.

`listPackagesFromCli` never inspects the exit code/`code` field of `execFileAsync` results (the helper resolves on failure too). A failed `pi list` silently yields an empty package list, and the error is only logged when a shell fallback is also attempted — if `direct` succeeds parsing but the shell retry path is skipped, or when `getShellCommand` returns null, real failures are swallowed and the UI shows zero packages instead of an error. Check `direct.code !== 0` / `fromShell.code !== 0` and surface the failure.

This duplication risks divergence (e.g. `getExtensionPath` vs the inline `e.path || ""` used in the buckets). `runPackageCommand` sets `loading: true` before spawning but only clears it on the 'close' and 'error' events. There is no timeout/kill guard, so if the child hangs or the streams stay open the promise never settles and the webview remains stuck in the loading state indefinitely. Add a timeout that kills the process (and clears loading) or otherwise guarantee the loading flag is reset.

comments.content: On the 'close' path the loading flag is cleared but the captured `output` from both streams is discarded when the exit code is 0, and on the error path the collected output is dropped entirely (only `err` is surfaced). Consider logging the collected output for diagnosability, and reset `output` handling consistently between the two terminal handlers.

`dispose()` fires a fire-and-forget IIFE that awaits `session_shutdown` and only then calls `session.dispose()`. Any code still holding the provider (or a pending `handleSessionEvent`) can reference a disposed session, and `this.session` stays set on the instance after `dispose()`, so a late `notifyWebview`/session call will operate on a torn-down runner. Consider clearing `this.session` and nulling listeners synchronously before the async emit, and guard the deferred `this.session!.dispose()` against the session having already been replaced.

If the debounced callback throws (e.g. `this.modelRuntime.refresh()` or `await this.refreshModels(false)` rejects), `resolve?.()` is never reached and `configRefreshPromise` is left dangling, so every future `handleExternalConfigChange` caller will await a promise that never resolves, permanently breaking config-change propagation. Also `resolve?.()` is called after the awaits but the local `resolve`/promise fields were already nulled, so a rejected refresh produces an unhandled rejection with no waiter notification. Wrap the body in try/finally and resolve (or reject) in the finally block.

`String(m.name)` is used for provider model names while `id` is cast with `String(m.id)` above; the filter already guarantees `m.id` is a string but `m.name` is only checked with `typeof m.name === "string"`. This is fine, but note the mixed typing: entry.id via `String(...)` vs entry.name conditional. No functional bug, but the `as Array<Record<string, unknown>>` cast plus per-field re-validation is duplicated logic that could be extracted. Consider a small mapper to reduce duplication with `fetchProviderModels` and `addProvider`.

`addProvider` persists the raw `apiKey` into models.json (plaintext, likely outside any credential store). This duplicates/leaks the secret into a config file that is also synced to the PI TUI and potentially checked into dotfile backups. Prefer delegating to the SDK credential store (e.g. `setRuntimeApiKey`/auth store) rather than writing secrets into models.json, or at minimum document why plaintext persistence is required.

`fetchProviderModels` sends the user-supplied API key as a Bearer token to an arbitrary `baseUrl` chosen by the caller. Since the URL is not validated (no scheme allowlist, unlike `openExternalUrl`), a typo or malicious value will leak the credential to an unintended host. Validate that the URL is http(s) and consider warning the user before transmitting secrets to user-provided endpoints.

`requestLoginPrompt` registers the resolver in `pendingLoginPrompts` *after* notifying the webview. If the webview answers synchronously (or the provider aborts) before the `new Promise` executor runs, `resolveLoginPrompt`/`rejectPendingLoginPrompts` will find no entry and silently drop the answer, leaving the login hanging until abort. Register the pending entry before sending `provider-login-prompt`, or re-check for a cancellation/abort signal after registration.

`editMessage` reaches into two private SDK APIs (`session._replaceMessageInPlace`, `sessionManager._rewriteFile`) with an unchecked `as any` cast. If either is absent in a newer SDK, the call throws or silently no-ops/corrupts the persisted transcript while the webview still shows the edited message. Add feature detection (`typeof ... === "function"`) with a clear error surfaced to the user instead of blindly calling private members.

`deleteSessions` emits `session_shutdown` with a hardcoded `reason: "new"` even when deleting the active session (the deleted session is being discarded, not started fresh), and it emits before disposing. This is inconsistent with `tearDownCurrentSession` which parameterizes the reason. Consider passing the correct reason so extensions can distinguish deletion from a new session.

The `configRefreshPromise` is stored as a field but the field is only assigned inside `handleExternalConfigChange`; if any other code path relies on it being non-null after resolution it would misbehave. More importantly, this promise is resolved with `resolve?.()` *after* the debounced callback's awaits are scheduled, so callers that `await handleExternalConfigChange(...)` may resume before `refreshModels` fully settles if a later `await` rejects. Guarantee settlement in a `finally` to keep the shared-promise contract reliable.

Prefix-suffix containment check is correct for the examples, but it does not resolve symlinks. Since `resolveMentionWithinRoot` only does a lexical check, a symlink inside the workspace (e.g. `link -> /etc`) is considered contained and `readMentionContext` will read files outside the root — the exact escape the comment says it prevents. Consider resolving the real path (e.g. `fs.realpathSync` on the resolved target and re-checking containment against the real root) or at least documenting that symlinks are not defended against.

comments.content: `isBinaryExtension` is fed the raw relative `mention.filePath` while existence is checked on the resolved `absPath`. For mentions of hidden/extension-less or case variants this works, but the binary check should be applied to the resolved path so the check and the file actually read refer to the same target. More importantly, there is no size guard before `fs.readFileSync`: a multi-GB file (even with a text extension) is read fully into memory before truncation, blocking the extension host. Stat/limit the size before reading, or read a capped amount.

Truncation compares `content.length` (UTF-16 code units) against `maxBytes` (50 * 1024), so multi-byte content can far exceed the intended 50KB budget and the "[file truncated at 50KB]" message is misleading. Additionally `content.slice(0, maxBytes)` may split a surrogate pair, producing a lone surrogate. Use `Buffer.byteLength` for the size check and guard against splitting surrogate pairs.

`resolvedText.replace(mention.match, "")` removes the first substring occurrence, not the occurrence at `mention.index`. If the same text appears earlier in the prompt (e.g. `@a.txt @a.txt` or a literal echo of the mention), the wrong occurrence is deleted, leaving the intended mention in the prompt and silently removing unrelated text. Replace using index/length (e.g. slice-based removal) instead of a global search by value.

The mention-regex captures everything up to whitespace, including trailing punctuation. A mention like `@file.ts,` or `@file.ts.` yields `filePath = "file.ts,"`, which fails `fs.existsSync` and is silently skipped (the mention is also not stripped from the prompt since `readMentionContext` returns null). Consider trimming/validating a plausible path (or handling common trailing punctuation) so valid mentions aren't dropped.

The JSDoc above `resolveFileMentions` is orphaned: it sits above `readMentionContext` (with its own doc comment immediately after), so it documents the wrong symbol and will be attributed to `readMentionContext`. Move it to directly precede `resolveFileMentions` or remove it.

Deduplication order gives precedence to the user settings: when a package source is later overridden by project settings, the project's install path is used only if `pkg.installedPath` is truthy, otherwise `existing?.path` (which is "" at this point for all entries) is used. Since all initial entries have `path: ""`, the fallback is effectively dead here, but the merge semantics are subtle. Confirm that project settings are intended to override user settings and make the precedence explicit.

`STROAGE_KEY_LAST_CHECK` is persisted before the pi/package checks are actually performed. If the check subsequently fails (network error, offline) or throws, the 1-hour throttle window is still consumed, so a legitimate retry is delayed for up to an hour. Move the timestamp update to after a successful check (or only on success).
